[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This guide defines how a single feature decomposes into the set of agent-ready GitHub issues — and their paired ADO User Stories — during Stage 10 of the architecture pipeline (GUID-GOV-PROC-016). It explains the routing labels, the backend `[layer]` chain, the per-screen `agent:ui` issues, and the dependency-tier sequencing that orders them. It is the reference behind what `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` produces.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#business-value]

### Business Value

- **Right-sized agent work** — each issue is one layer or one screen, small enough that an agent completing "the whole issue" is correct, rather than one oversized issue spanning a full stack.
- **Deterministic sequencing without hand-built dependency graphs** — the order in which issues become workable falls out of declared dependency tiers (T1/T2/T3), not manual wiring.
- **No silently-skipped layers** — UI is a first-class routing label (`agent:ui`), so the Presentation layer is dispatched and tracked like any other.
page_texts.6:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#scope-and-applicability]

### Scope and Applicability

Applies to any project at Stage 10 of the pipeline. A trivial feature may decompose into as few as two issues (implementation + testing); a deep, UI-bearing feature fans into a backend `[layer]` chain, one UI issue per screen, testing, and infrastructure — each sequenced behind the **container foundations** (UI app shell, cloud environment, component scaffold, test harness) it shares with its sibling features.

**Skill attribution**: `/architect`, `/deployer`, and `/tester` referenced throughout this guidance are Skills owned and invoked by the **consuming product repository** executing this pipeline (e.g., an eap-bootstrap-derived project) — `eap-ref-architecture` does not itself define or invoke `/deployer` or `/tester`.
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#a-feature-is-a-vertical-slice]

### A feature is a vertical slice

A feature rarely lives in one layer. A capability like *compare jurisdictions side-by-side* cuts through infrastructure, a data/read model, a domain service, a backend-for-frontend, a dashboard screen, and tests. Treating "the feature" as one issue produces an oversized, hard-to-review unit and hides the real sequencing. Decomposing by layer makes each unit small, independently reviewable, and correctly ordered.
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#routing-labels]

### Routing labels

| Label | Layer it covers |
|-------|-----------------|
| `agent:implementation` | Backend / data / service / **served HTTP API** — non-UI `scope=code` work (produces the API that BFFs and other contexts consume) |
| `agent:ui` | A Presentation-layer screen governed by a UI Contract (one issue per screen), **including the screen's co-located BFF data-shaping route** |
| `agent:testing` | Tests for an implementation or UI issue (incl. `contract` provider verification against shared endpoint contracts) |
| `agent:infrastructure` | Cloud resources from `scope=infra` constraints |

`agent:ui` is a first-class peer of the other routing labels — the same dispatch, ownership, and separation-of-duties rules apply (a UI agent owns the Presentation component path and nothing else).

**There is deliberately no `agent:bff` label.** The BFF is per-experience data-shaping owned by the frontend (industry standard — Sam Newman, "one experience, one BFF"; Microsoft Azure Architecture Center, "frontend teams independently manage their own BFF"). A separate BFF agent would recreate the centralized-backend bottleneck the pattern exists to remove. The BFF route is therefore **folded into the `agent:ui` screen issue** (the frontend owns it), and the *backend* produces the **API the BFF consumes** — not the BFF itself. The BFF holds only client-specific shaping; domain logic stays in the backend API.
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#the-decomposition]

### The decomposition

For each feature, `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` produces:

1. **Backend implementation** — one `agent:implementation` issue by default. For a fresh component (declared `Foundation = Yes`), an `[scaffold]` foundation issue is emitted once and precedes everything else. When the file-count/complexity heuristic trips for a deep slice, the implementation expands into an **ordered `[layer]` chain** (a title/scope convention, not new labels):
   - `[scaffold]` — component project scaffold (once per component; reused thereafter)
   - `[data]` — read model / persistence / query path — `prereq(T1): [scaffold]`
   - `[service]` — domain logic — `prereq(T1): [data]`
   - `[api]` — the **served HTTP API** exposing the service over the endpoints consumers bind to — `prereq(T1): [service]`. Its scope (method/path/response) is **generated from the shared endpoint contract** authored at design time (GUID-GOV-PROC-014 / logical-arch Phase 4.5), not from the behavioral `.feature`. The `[bff]` layer is **not** a backend spine layer — the BFF is owned by the frontend and folded into the UI screen issue (see routing labels above).
2. **UI (with its BFF folded in)** — for a `@UI` feature, one **app-foundation** `agent:ui` issue per app (once), then **one `agent:ui` issue per screen** in the UI Contract, each gated on an `approved` contract (GUID-GOV-PROC-014) and `prereq(T1)` on its app foundation. Each screen issue also **implements the screen's BFF data-shaping route**, verified against the binding's shared endpoint contract; it is `prereq(T2)` (default) on the **backend API** the BFF consumes. Screen issues are idempotent by the stable ID `<contractId>-<screenId>` — on re-run, existing issues are reused, not duplicated.
3. **Testing** — one `agent:testing` issue per implementation/UI issue. Its prerequisites are **test-type-specific**, read from the `## Test Strategy` table (see "Test prerequisites by type" below) — not a flat "T1 on the implementation". A per-type **harness foundation** (`TEST-HARNESS-<type>`) is emitted once per test type and is a T1 prerequisite of every test issue covering that type.
4. **Infrastructure** — one `agent:infrastructure` issue per concern when `scope=infra` constraints exist, plus one **environment-foundation** issue per `IAC-FOUNDATION-<env>` (once). Each concern infrastructure issue is `prereq(T1)` on its environment foundation.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#test-prerequisites-by-type]

### Test prerequisites by type

PROC-015 keeps **one `agent:testing` issue per implementation/UI issue** — the test type does *not* change the issue count. What it changes is the **prerequisites and acceptance criteria inside that one issue**, looked up from the `## Test Strategy` table. The flat "testing is T1 on the thing it tests" is the **unit-test special case**; other types differ:

| Test type | Harness foundation | Target prereq (tier) | Env prereq |
|-----------|--------------------|-----------------------|------------|
| unit | jest/pytest/cargo | impl (T1) | none |
| component | jest + RTL + jest-axe | screen (T1) | UI app foundation (T1) |
| integration | testcontainers/compose | modules under test (T1) | environment foundation (T1) |
| contract | Pact/registry | producer **interface (T2)** | broker/registry (T1) |
| e2e | Playwright + test-server | app foundation + screens + backend, **live** (T1) | environment foundation (T1) |
| load / chaos | k6 / chaos tooling | — (SUT exists) | environment foundation + observability (T1) |
| architecture | ArchUnit/NetArchTest | — (**static**) | none |

A single UI screen's test issue therefore carries *both* component prerequisites (component harness, the screen, the app foundation) *and* e2e prerequisites (Playwright harness, live backend, the environment foundation) — several prerequisite lines in **one** issue.

[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#foundations-foundation-before-fan-out]

### Foundations (foundation-before-fan-out)

A feature decomposes into siblings *within* a layer — many screens of one app, many concerns' infrastructure, many features of one service. Those siblings frequently **share a scaffold that is built once per container**, and that scaffold is invisible to the feature/data dependency edges. If it is left implicit, every sibling looks independently dispatchable, and N agents each re-create — and collide on — the same scaffold from a cold start (e.g. 21 dashboard screens each scaffolding the same Next.js shell; 9 concerns' infrastructure each bootstrapping the same Terraform state and cluster).

The rule: **whenever a layer fans out into N siblings that share a once-per-container scaffold, that scaffold is an explicit `foundation` the siblings depend on (T1).** The container fans out as **foundation (1) → siblings (parallel) → tests**, never flat-N from a cold start. There are **six** foundation-bearing containers — the last two are cross-cutting-concern foundations (see the Seam Contract section):

| Container | Foundation (built once) | Fan-out siblings | Declared in (logical architecture) |
|-----------|-------------------------|------------------|-------------------------------------|
| **UI app** | app shell, providers, routing/nav, design tokens, BFF client | screens | `kind:"foundation"` UI Contract (GUID-GOV-PROC-014) |
| **Cloud environment** | Terraform remote state, root module, VPC, cluster, baseline IAM/KMS | per-concern infrastructure | `IAC-FOUNDATION-<env>` row in the Infrastructure section |
| **Code component** | package manifest, DI container, base config, conventions | a fresh component's feature implementations | `Foundation = Yes` on the component table; emitted as an `[scaffold]` issue preceding `[data]` |
| **Test harness** (per type) | runner + config for each test type (jest, Playwright, testcontainers, k6, ArchUnit) | every test of that type | `## Test Strategy` table (per `testType`) |
| **Auth / access-control** | service-level authn token validation, RBAC/authz enforcement, 401/403 RFC 7807 envelope | every served-API/feature whose endpoints are in the policy's scope | `Scope = platform` Security-Layer rows governed by a **cross-cutting Rego policy** (policy-as-code) → `AUTH-FOUNDATION` |
| **Observability** | structured audit-log emission, metric + trace instrumentation conventions | every feature impl that must emit audit logs/metrics/traces | `Scope = platform` observability rows → `OBS-FOUNDATION` |

Foundations are **declared in the logical architecture**, which precedes export (GUID-GOV-PROC-016) — so `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` reads a declared marker and emits the T1 edge deterministically; it never infers a foundation from repo state. If a container has fan-out siblings but no declared foundation, export **halts** with an instruction to declare it (`/eap-decom-logical-arch-modify`) rather than guessing. Each foundation issue is emitted once (idempotent by its stable ID) and reused as the prerequisite for every sibling.

**Emission trigger — the first sibling that needs it emits it.** A foundation issue is not created by a separate step; it is emitted by the **first fan-out sibling that references it**, then reused. The first concern infrastructure issue emits its `IAC-FOUNDATION-<env>`; the first feature implementation of a fresh component emits its `[scaffold]`; the first `@UI` feature of an app emits its app-shell issue; and the **first `agent:testing` issue covering a given `testType` emits that type's `TEST-HARNESS-<type>` setup issue** (then references it). This matters most for the test harness, because a test issue covers its types implicitly (a UI screen's test covers `component` + `e2e`, so it emits both harness issues on first encounter) — the harness issue must be created at that point, not assumed to exist. In every case the foundation issue exists before the `Prerequisite (T1)` edge that points at it.

**Adopting the model mid-flight (back-fill on re-run).** A project whose siblings were exported *before* a foundation was declared will have fan-out issues missing their `Prerequisite (T1): <foundation>` line, and the foundation issue may not yet exist — the common state when a team adopts foundation-before-fan-out after an initial export. `/eap-sdd-health-check` flags this. **Re-running `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` reconciles it idempotently**: it emits any missing foundation issue (search by stable ID first) and patches each pre-existing sibling in place to add the missing prerequisite (for test issues, replacing any blanket "T1 on impl" line with the Test Strategy-table prerequisites) — no duplicate siblings. Follow with `/eap-decom-spec-plan-sequence --reconcile` to refresh the plan's layer edges and `/eap-sdd-health-check` to confirm closure.

[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#the-deliverable-identity-spine-linkage-status-idempotency]

### The deliverable-identity spine (linkage, status, idempotency)

Every emitted issue carries a **full stable-ID** — not only foundations and screens (`<contractId>-<screenId>`) but backend impl/test too (`<concern>-<feature-slug>[-<layer>]`). This single identity is the key that keeps the execution graph coherent end-to-end, consumed at four points a decomposed issue would otherwise lose:

- **Emission (dedupe on re-run).** `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` searches by the full stable-ID before creating any issue and reuses the match, so a re-run against a growing spec set reuses the whole fan-out — not just foundations/screens — instead of duplicating it.
- **Linkage (issue ↔ PR ↔ commit).** Agent PRs run `auto-close-issue: false` (an issue may fan into multiple PRs), so the issue→commit link is recovered from the **`agent/<issue>-<slug>` branch name** (stored PR metadata — survives branch deletion) and reinforced by a `Refs #<issue>` line in the PR body. This is what lets a merged PR's commit be stamped into `Built-From` (the "what shipped" anchor) with no human step.
- **Status transition on close.** When `/eap-decom-spec-plan-sequence --reconcile` (with `--dispatch`) closes an issue whose PR merged, it transitions the paired traceability row `specified → implemented` (impl close) or `→ verified` (test close) — so the matrix reflects shipped reality rather than staying `specified` forever (which otherwise corrupts `--skip-implemented`). Completeness is a `/project-manager` judgment: a multi-PR deliverable is not "done" on its first merge.
- **Idempotency of *execution* (not just emission).** The same identity de-duplicates *agent runs* at three points, all keyed on the **full** stable-ID so distinct layers/screens of one contract are never treated as duplicates: a **pre-dispatch gate** (if the deliverable already shipped under a sibling issue, do not dispatch — label `agent:duplicate`, comment `superseded by #<canonical>`, close not-planned); an **agent no-op-with-provenance** (a worker that finds the named deliverable already fully built no-ops with provenance rather than opening a redundant PR; a partial build proceeds; ambiguity routes to `/eap-spec-loopback`); and a **duplicate-cluster collapse** in reconcile (group by full stable-ID, keep the canonical member carrying a resolved `Built-From`, close the rest — never collapsing a genuine multi-layer/multi-screen deliverable, whose members have *distinct* stable-IDs).

[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#dependency-tier-sequencing-t1t2t3]

### Dependency-tier sequencing (T1/T2/T3)

Issues are ordered by prerequisite tiers, not a hand-built graph. The tier expresses *what must exist before this issue can start*:

| Tier | Meaning | Blocks until… |
|------|---------|---------------|
| **T1** | Runtime dependency — needs the producer's live behavior/data | the producer issue is **merged** |
| **T2** | Interface/contract dependency — can build against the contract or a stub | the producer's **interface exists** |
| **T3** | Data-state dependency — satisfiable by fixtures/mocks | never blocks |

Within the backend spine: `[service]` is T1 on `[data]`; `[api]` (served HTTP API) is T1 on `[service]`. Testing is always T1 on the thing it tests.
page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#uibackend-sequencing-comes-from-the-ui-contract--bound-to-a-shared-endpoint-contract]

### UI→backend sequencing comes from the UI Contract — bound to a shared endpoint contract

The authoritative source of a UI issue's prerequisite is the UI Contract's `dataBindings` — each binding declares its `producingService`, its `dependencyTier`, and a **`contractRef` to a shared endpoint contract** (the design-time OpenAPI + response-schema artifact both sides bind to — GUID-GOV-PROC-014). `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` emits the prerequisite line from that:

- **T2** (default) — the screen (and its folded BFF route) builds against the backend API's shared contract or a stub; dispatch once the interface exists. **A T2 binding is DONE only when the producer is built, served, and passes contract verification** against `contractRef` — a permanent stub is not a satisfied T2 (arch-health-check runtime-cohesion gate enforces this).
- **T1** — the screen needs live data to be built or verified; wait for the producer to merge.

This means UI sequencing is declared in the contract, not inferred — and the *shape* is a shared schema, not a per-side invention, so the UI/BFF agent and the API agent cannot drift. See GUID-GOV-PROC-014.

**Consumer-driven contract correlation.** The shared endpoint contract is what makes the piecewise agent hand-off produce composable code: it is authored once at design time, `$ref`'d by the UI Contract binding (consumer), used to *generate* the backend `[api]` issue (producer), and verified from both sides. Without it, independently-dispatched agents each author their own request/response shape and drift — the failure mode where UI screens ship against stubs whose real providers are never built.
page_texts.17:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#seams-are-the-second-decomposition-axis-edges-not-just-nodes]

### Seams are the second decomposition axis (edges, not just nodes)

The `[api]`↔UI seam above is one instance of a general law: **behavioral (`.feature`) decomposition builds *nodes* (capabilities) but is blind to *edges*** — the contracts, glue, wiring, and cross-cutting policy that join nodes. An edge has no behavioral scenario of its own, so it decomposes into no work item and each adjacent node's tests pass with the other side stubbed. This is why the BFF/API seam was silently unbuilt, and it recurs for **async event seams** and **cross-cutting policy seams** (auth, observability) unless they are made first-class too.

The **Seam Contract** (authored at `/eap-decom-logical-arch-create` Phase 4.5, in the **native industry standard** for its class — the pipeline defines no custom contract format) is the artifact that promotes every edge to a first-class citizen, symmetric with how a `.feature` promotes a capability. Three classes:

| Seam class | Native standard | Producer owner | Consumer |
|------------|-----------------|----------------|----------|
| `sync-api` | **OpenAPI 3.1** (`.../<service>/openapi.json`, operation by `operationId`) | `[api]` issue (generated from the operation) / folded BFF in `agent:ui` | UI binding (`contractRef` JSON-Pointer) or another BC |
| `event` | **AsyncAPI 3.0** (`.../events/<service>.asyncapi.json`) | publishing BC's `agent:implementation` (real publisher, not a stub/dead-code builder) | subscribing BC(s) — a produced topic with zero consumers is a FAIL |
| `cross-cutting` | **OPA/Rego** (policy-as-code; 401/403 shapes in the sync-api OpenAPI docs) | `AUTH-FOUNDATION` / `OBS-FOUNDATION` cross-cutting foundation | every feature in the policy's scope (T1 prereq) |

Producer/consumer identity rides as native `x-` specification extensions (`x-producer`/`x-consumers`) on each operation; dependency tier lives on the consumer's UI Contract binding, not the producer operation (the same producer can be T1 for one consumer, T2 for another). A seam is **built iff both its producer is served and its consumer is wired** — `/eap-sdd-health-check` **Phase 11 (Seam Cohesion)** verifies this for all three classes (the runtime backstop), and `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` **halts** if a declared seam (a UI binding, an event topic in the integration table, or a `Scope = platform` auth constraint) has no resolving contract. This is design-first consumer-driven-contract testing (industry standard — OpenAPI/AsyncAPI + Rego + Pact/CDC), authored upfront because isolated agents cannot converge emergently. The standard is chosen for the *human* reviewer (recognize a known format, low onboarding); the AI coding agent consumes whatever artifact it is pointed at.
page_texts.18:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#the-cross-cutting-class-is-policy-as-code-oparego--with-a-design-vs-agent-ownership-split]

#### The `cross-cutting` class is policy-as-code (OPA/Rego) — with a design-vs-agent ownership split

The `cross-cutting` seam class (authz/RBAC and related policy invariants that span nodes) is authored as **policy-as-code in OPA/Rego** — CNCF-graduated, the same engine that governs RBAC/authz, IaC/Terraform-plan validation, K8s admission (Gatekeeper), and CI/CD gates. It is **not** authn (identity mechanism → OpenAPI `securitySchemes` / the IdP), not the error envelope (→ the sync-api OpenAPI RFC 7807 shapes), and not observability (→ the OBS-FOUNDATION container).

Because an authz rule is a **negative/compliance invariant**, its authorship is split so that no agent writes the policy meant to constrain it:

| Concern | Owner | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Policy **decision** + **Rego rules** | **human-directed design** — `/architect`, `/eap-decom-logical-arch-create` Phase 6 | fox-guarding-henhouse: an agent must not author the invariant that gates its own output |
| Enforcement **wiring** (OPA sidecar / gateway / Gatekeeper / CI gate — the `AUTH-FOUNDATION` issue) | **agent output** — the consuming repository's own `/deployer` Skill (owns IaC/CICD) | mechanical integration of a decided policy |
| **Verification** | **both** — `opa test` on the Rego + a property/fitness check that no in-scope endpoint bypasses it | the invariant must be proven, not asserted |

**No new command or skill** is introduced — a dedicated policy-authoring command would re-skin the standard (the same custom-wrapper anti-pattern the native-standards correction removed) and destroy the onboarding value (a reviewer already knows Rego). The pipeline reuses `/architect` (decision), the consuming repository's own `/deployer` Skill (wiring), and its own `/tester` Skill + native `opa test` (verification). The `policy` test type in the `## Test Strategy` table is operational when `opa`/`conftest` is installed and invoked in CI (checked by `/eap-sdd-health-check` Phase 10 Step 4).

[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#the-full-decomposition-axis-taxonomy-what-behavioral-feature-files-drop-and-how-each-is-owned]

### The full decomposition-axis taxonomy (what behavioral `.feature` files drop, and how each is owned)

Gherkin specifies *observable functional behavior, at a single boundary, at a point in time, for one actor, via enumerated examples.* Each clause it does **not** cover is an axis that decomposition silently drops — and each is closed by the same triad (design-time artifact in the native standard → injected into the agent-task issue → PR-failing gate), reusing existing skills, adding **no new command or skill**:

| Axis | What Gherkin drops | Native artifact (design-time) | Gate (`/eap-sdd-health-check`) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Behavior (node)** | — (this is what it covers) | `.feature` | Phase 2 tag continuity |
| **Seam (edge)** | "single boundary" | OpenAPI / AsyncAPI / Rego (per class) | Phase 11 seam cohesion |
| **Negative / universal property** | "enumerated examples" — can't say "for all / never" | **Invariants register** (`logical-arch` Phase 8) routed to `architecture` (fitness: import-linter/dependency-cruiser/NetArchTest) or `property` (PBT: Hypothesis/proptest/fast-check) tiers — no custom artifact | Phase 5 Step 5 (invariant has a tier + operational harness) + Phase 10 Step 4 (tier operational) |
| **NFR / operational** | "functional behavior" — load/latency/chaos need generators, not one run | `REQ-NFR-*` (exists) + a `TEST-HARNESS-<type>` that is actually **operational** (scaffold + CI invocation; binary runners k6/opa via a CI setup step, not a manifest dep) | Phase 10 Step 4 (declared type must be built + invoked in CI) |
| **Data model (shared entities)** | implicit "given data exists" — no owner of the canonical model | **Canonical `_components/` JSON-Schema library** (`logical-arch` Phase 3): a shape used by ≥2 BCs is authored once and `$ref`'d, never inlined; `Owning Context` = the DDD context-map / published-language owner | Phase 8 Step 3 (shared entity: one canonical def, `$ref`'d not inlined, no drift, one owner) |
| **Journey (cross-BC path)** | "one actor/capability" — a path through ≥2 BCs is owned by no node | **Arazzo** document (`logical-arch` Phase 4.6) composing existing seam operations into an ordered workflow — only for *genuine* cross-BC paths, never an intra-service stage pipeline | Phase 11 Step 5 (every step resolves to a built/served producer — the whole path is walkable) |

The recurring failure these close is identical: *no scenario → no artifact → no owning work item → no gate → built by no one.* The template owns the slot, the shape (a recognized standard), and the gate; the project owns the standard's content. **Data-model note:** inlining a shared shape into N per-service seam docs re-opens the drift it was meant to prevent — the `_components/` library is the single source of truth, `$ref`'d by relative path from every seam that uses it.
page_texts.21:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#one-issue--one-story--one-layer]

### One issue ↔ one Story ↔ one layer

Each issue produced here is paired 1:1 with an ADO User Story under the feature's ADO Feature (`/eap-decom-spec-export-boards --stories`). The layer qualifier (`impl`, `impl:service`, `ui:<screen>`, `test`, `ui-test:<screen>`, `infra`) is applied consistently across the GitHub issue, the ADO Story, and the traceability matrix so the trace is unambiguous. See GUID-GOV-PROC-007 for the ADO side.
page_texts.22:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#no-within-issue-pacing]

### No within-issue pacing

Because each issue is one layer/screen and the DAG sequences them, there is no need for "do X before Y" pacing language inside an issue. The issue stays whole-and-small; the prerequisite tiers pace the feature.
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#worked-example--compare-jurisdictions-ui-bearing-deep-backend]

### Worked example — "Compare jurisdictions" (UI-bearing, deep backend)

```
Feature: Compare jurisdictions          → ADO Feature
   (foundations — emitted once per container, shared across features)
   ◆ agent:infrastructure  IAC-FOUNDATION-dev (state, VPC, cluster)  prereq: —
   ◆ agent:ui              AnalyticalDashboard app foundation        prereq(T2): BFF interface
   ◆ agent:implementation  [scaffold] analysis component             prereq: —
   (this feature's slice)
├─ agent:infrastructure  comparison query infra        prereq(T1): IAC-FOUNDATION-dev
├─ agent:implementation  [data] comparison read model  prereq(T1): [scaffold]
├─ agent:implementation  [service] comparison endpoint  prereq(T1): [data]
├─ agent:implementation  [api] dashboard aggregation     prereq(T2): [service]
├─ agent:ui              comparison dashboard screen     prereq(T1): app foundation; prereq(T2): [api]
├─ agent:testing         service tests (unit+integration) prereq(T1): [service]; integration also prereq(T1): IAC-FOUNDATION-dev
└─ agent:testing         UI screen tests (component+e2e)  prereq(T1): ui screen + app foundation; e2e also prereq(T1): IAC-FOUNDATION-dev
```

The foundations (◆) are emitted **once** and reused by every feature of that app/environment/component — they are not re-created per feature. Concern infrastructure is **not** parallel-from-cold: it waits on the environment foundation (the earlier "(parallel) prereq: —" guidance was incorrect — it let N concerns collide on the same Terraform state and cluster).
page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-015-vertical-slice-decomposition-guide.md#worked-example--trivial-feature]

### Worked example — trivial feature

```
Feature: Maintain waiver inventory       → ADO Feature
├─ agent:implementation  maintain inventory  prereq(T1): [scaffold] (if component is fresh; else —)
└─ agent:testing         inventory tests      prereq(T1): implementation   (unit only)
```

No `[layer]` chain, no UI — the complexity heuristic did not trip, so the backend stays one issue. If its component was already scaffolded by an earlier feature, even the `[scaffold]` prerequisite is already satisfied and the slice is just two issues. The test issue is unit-only, so the flat "T1 on implementation" rule applies directly.

Closes the gap where UI shipped against stubs whose providers were never built |
| 1.3.0 | 2026-07-07 | James Macurak | **Systemic generalization — "seams are the second decomposition axis" (behavioral decomposition builds nodes, not edges).** BFF confirmed as the first instance of a class also affecting async **event** seams and **cross-cutting** (auth/observability) seams. Grounded in OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/CloudEvents + Pact/CDC (design-first, adapted for agent isolation) |
| 1.4.0 | 2026-07-07 | James Macurak | **Seam contracts authored in native standards (custom wrapper retired).** Each seam class now uses its native, purpose-built standard instead of the custom `seam-contract.schema.json` wrapper: `sync-api` → **OpenAPI 3.1** (per-service `openapi.json`), `event` → **AsyncAPI 3.0** (per-service `.asyncapi.json`), `cross-cutting` → **OPA/Rego** (policy-as-code). Pipeline metadata rides as native `x-` extensions; the UI `contractRef` is a JSON-Pointer into an OpenAPI operation. Rationale: a custom catch-all format forces reviewers to learn a bespoke DSL; use the minimal coherent family of recognized standards (OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/Rego + JSON Schema for embedded shapes) — the standard is for the human, the agent consumes what it is pointed at. Companion: GUID-GOV-PROC-016 v1.6, GUID-GOV-PROC-014 v1.3 |
| 1.5.0 | 2026-07-07 | James Macurak | **Policy-as-code (OPA/Rego) for the `cross-cutting` seam class, with a design-vs-agent ownership split.** The cross-cutting class (authz/RBAC and related invariants) is authored as Rego: the policy **decision + rules** are human-directed design (`/architect`, `/eap-decom-logical-arch-create` Phase 6 — an agent must not author the invariant gating its own output); enforcement **wiring** is agent output (`/deployer`, the `AUTH-FOUNDATION` issue); **verification** is both (`opa test` + a no-bypass fitness check). **No new command or skill** — reuse `/architect`/`/deployer`/`/tester` + native `opa test`; a `policy` test type in the Test Strategy table (operational when `opa`/`conftest` is in CI, per `/eap-sdd-health-check` Phase 10 Step 4). | 1.6.0 | 2026-07-07 | James Macurak | **Complete the decomposition-axis taxonomy — negative/property, NFR-operational, data-model, and journey axes.** After on-disk audit of the exemplar (all four confirmed real + unowned), add each as the same triad (native artifact → issue injection → PR gate), no new command/skill: **negative/property** = an Invariants register (logical-arch Phase 8) routed to `architecture`/`property` tiers with a Phase 5 Step 5 + Phase 10 Step 4 gate; **NFR-operational** = a `TEST-HARNESS-<type>` that must be *operational* (scaffold + CI invocation; binary-runner detection fix); **data-model** = a canonical `_components/` JSON-Schema library (`$ref`'d not inlined) + DDD context-map (Owning Context) with a Phase 8 Step 3 consistency gate — also corrects the regression where folding `_components/` per-service re-opened cross-BC drift; **journey** = Arazzo docs composing seam operations (logical-arch Phase 4.6, genuine cross-BC paths only) with a Phase 11 Step 5 path-cohesion gate. Companion: GUID-GOV-PROC-016 v1.8, `/eap-decom-logical-arch-create` Phases 3/4.5/4.6/8, `arch-health-check` Phases 5/8/10/11, `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` | Enhancement — closes the remaining lossy decomposition axes; no breaking change to shipped artifacts (adds gates + a canonical-model rule) |
| 1.7.0 | 2026-07-08 | James Macurak | **Change propagation + drift detection (the maintenance direction).** A change at any SDLC stage flows one-way into new downstream work, and neither spec nor code drifts silently: (1) governed modify front doors for every artifact type (`/eap-decom-logical-arch-modify` extended to seam/policy/journey/`_components`; `/eap-decom-ui-contract-modify`) — prose intent in, command writes+version-bumps, never a hand-edit or the agent; (2) forward-only emission — a change emits a NEW superseding issue (`Built-From`/`Supersedes` chain, SemVer + merge-commit anchor), the shipped issue never reopened, cross-layer changes fan into the layered change spine; (3) `arch-health-check --drift` — ungoverned-hand-edit detector (version-bump check, any author) + shipped-implementation freshness (git diff from built-from commit) + agent-PR fast-fail. Reuses existing skills; no new command (a `/eap-defect` alias routes bugs through the same path). Companion: GUID-GOV-PROC-016 v1.9, GUID-GOV-PROC-014 v1.4 | Enhancement — closes the change-propagation + bidirectional-drift gaps; additive |
| 1.8.0 | 2026-07-10 | James Macurak | **The deliverable-identity spine — linkage, status-on-close, universal stable-ID, and execution idempotency (mirrors the eap-bootstrap maintenance-edge + idempotency build).** The full stable-ID now keys **all** issue types (backend impl/test `<concern>-<feature-slug>[-<layer>]`, not just screens), consumed at four points: (1) **emission dedupe** — re-run reuses the whole fan-out by stable-ID, not only foundations/screens; (2) **linkage** — issue↔PR↔commit recovered from the `agent/<issue>-<slug>` branch name (survives branch deletion) + a `Refs #<issue>` PR-body line, feeding the `Built-From` merge-commit anchor with no human step; (3) **status-on-close** — `/eap-decom-spec-plan-sequence --reconcile --dispatch` transitions the traceability row `specified→implemented`/`→verified` on issue close (a `/project-manager` completeness call; multi-PR ≠ done), so the matrix stops reading `specified` for shipped work and no longer corrupts `--skip-implemented`; (4) **execution idempotency** — pre-dispatch gate (skip + `agent:duplicate` + close-not-planned if the deliverable already shipped), agent no-op-with-provenance for an already-built deliverable, and duplicate-cluster collapse in reconcile — all keyed on the **full** stable-ID so distinct layers/screens are never collapsed. Also records that Phase-12 shipped-freshness judges staleness by **version comparison**, not raw `git diff` (same-version governed migrations are not drift). Companion: GUID-GOV-PROC-016 v1.10, GUID-GOV-PROC-014 v1.5 | Enhancement — makes the change-propagation model operational (linkage/status) and adds execution idempotency; additive |
